A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EquivaMap and EquivaFormulation. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and matchable, including the additional appendices in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original equivalence-classification experiments on EquivaFormulation in Tables 2–4, including comparisons with four baselines and LP/MILP breakdowns.

after.justification: v2 retains the original accuracy experiments and adds measured component and total runtimes in Appendix D, Table 5.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same LLM mapping discovery, solution mapping, feasibility/optimality checks, and aggregation procedure. Both prompt listings are unchanged. The new discussion of symbolic formulations and variable sets documents the procedure more explicitly; it does not establish an implemented method change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same NLP4LP-derived EquivaFormulation problems and transformation categories. The new runtime analysis uses that dataset. Appendix C illustrates the maximum independent set problem already used in Figure 1; it introduces no additional evaluated dataset or scenario.

E2.justification: Canonical accuracy, execution accuracy, WL-test, and naive-LLM remain the comparators in all corresponding accuracy tables. The new runtime comparison measures two existing baselines, execution accuracy and WL-test; it neither introduces a new comparison method nor removes a baseline from an existing experiment.

E3.justification: Appendix D adds evaluation of per-instance runtime, separating solving, LLM calls, and WL-test computation and averaging over the dataset. The accuracy protocol retains GPT-4, K = 3, the same instance counts, feasibility filtering, and formulation perturbations. No rerun or modification of those accuracy experiments is established.

E4.justification: The new runtime breakdown investigates computational overhead and identifies LLM interaction as the dominant cost. Existing transformation-based evaluations and LP/MILP analyses remain unchanged. Appendix C is an explanatory representation example, not a new measured robustness test or ablation.

E5.justification: Table 5 introduces mean ± standard deviation reporting for runtimes across dataset instances. Accuracy reporting remains percentages and raw counts, and K = 3 is unchanged. No additional seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or timing repetition count is provided.

E6.justification: All existing accuracy entries in Tables 2–4 are unchanged. New Table 5 reports total runtimes of 0.12 ± 0.02 seconds for execution accuracy, 0.38 ± 0.07 for WL-test, and 12.00 ± 4.50 for EquivaMap, including 11.88 ± 4.48 for LLM calls. Section 4.2 broadens its baseline-failure wording, but supplies no changed accuracy results.

T1.justification: Definition 3.5 changes its statement from the two formulations being equivalent to α′ being equivalent to α and explicitly disclaims symmetry. A new branch-and-bound example distinguishes polynomial-time construction of a mapping from polynomial-time evaluation. The three mathematical requirements remain unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction add an explicit claim that the verification stage ensures feasibility and optimality without additional MILP solver calls. This foregrounds a property of the retained procedure. The principal claims about Quasi-Karp equivalence, the first equivalent-formulation dataset, and superior classification performance remain.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 newly distinguishes formulation-level symbolic mappings from instance-specific verification, while Appendix C explains scalability through variable-set representations. Appendix D acknowledges higher runtime, identifies the LLM bottleneck, and argues that offline use can tolerate the cost. The existing limitation concerning simple transformations and omitted complex reformulations is retained.

D1.justification: Section 3.3 and Appendix C newly document retaining symbolic parameters, describing each variable set once, and the corresponding JSON representation. Appendix D supplies component runtimes but omits hardware and timing repetition details. Existing prompt listings and code/data destinations are unchanged; the dataset link is merely relocated to the first-page footnote.

R1.justification: The same 39 referenced works and substantive related-work positioning are retained. Changes to publication years and Karp's bibliographic entry concern metadata for existing works. The introduction's mention of human effort in constructing reductions elaborates the existing automation motivation.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract and selected introductory passages, retitles Section 3.3, reorders its explanations, and separates the existing prompts into Appendix B. It adds Appendices C and D and makes localized language and bibliographic edits. Most of the document and both prompt listings remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 3 comparing input representations and Table 5 presenting runtimes. It expands Figure 1's caption, numbers Algorithm 1's lines, and shifts table and paragraph placement. The original figure artwork and existing table structures are retained, so this is a limited presentation revision.

improvement.justification: The runtime breakdown makes a previously unquantified accuracy–cost tradeoff assessable, while the directional definition and symbolic-input explanations improve clarity. These are useful but limited gains: the algorithm and accuracy evidence are unchanged, timing hardware and repetition details remain unspecified, and the broader baseline-failure wording should not be read as a new category-level result.
